text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service:euw-frontend (az7) reporting elevated 5xx and connection resets over IPv6. Aggregated spike started ~1768501100. Sample symptoms: TLS handshake failures, high SYN retries, and sustained RTT >2000ms for some flows. Incident ID INC-20260315-az7-1768501123. Paging oncall-eu.

oncall-eu: on it. I see spike in errors on the LB metrics dashboard. Rolling up logs now.

neteng: pulling tcpdump on az7-lb4 now. Early hint: lots of "ICMPv6 Packet too big" from upstream router, followed by client retransmits. Possible PMTUD path MTU blackhole.

platform-sre: confirming from edge: users behind certain mobile networks see failures over IPv6 but succeed over IPv4. That aligns with PMTUD issues.

oncall-eu: running quick traceroute6 from probe to service:
```
traceroute to 2001:db8::service (2606:xxxx:xxxx::1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  2001:db8::gw (2001:db8::gw)  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 2  2a02:xxxx:edge (2a02:xxxx:edge)  12.3 ms  12.1 ms  12.0 ms
 3  * * *  (frag needed?)
```
Looks like last hop doesn't respond to larger probes.

neteng: confirmed via tcpdump: ICMPv6 Type 2 "Packet too big" with MTU=1280 being returned, but devices upstream drop packets with DF set so PMTUD fails. Classic blackhole when jumbo frames expected.

support-ops: pulling list of customers impacted. Early estimate: ~11-14% of EU sessions using IPv6 see increased errors, especially mobile and some ISP ranges.

oncall-eu: quick mitigation idea: enable TCP MSS clamping at LB to 1220 to avoid large segments; also add temporary route weights to shift non-critical customer traffic off az7 to az6. Thoughts?

neteng: agree. Applying MSS clamp on az7-lb4 ingress now. Command:
```
# on linux edge hosts
iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Applied to load balancer fleet in az7.

platform-sre: also opening emergency route policy change to reduce traffic to az7 by 40% for non-SLA customers via smart routing. Will execute in 2 mins.

support-ops: status page draft: "We are experiencing increased errors for some customers in EU due to IPv6 path MTU issues affecting one Availability Zone. Engineers are mitigating." Should I publish?

oncall-eu: publish with impact: "Some users on IPv6 may see timeouts or failures; we have mitigations in place; full remediation in progress." Go ahead. :thumbsup:

support-ops: published. status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-1768501123 updated.

neteng: MSS clamp rolled out to 100% of az7 LBs. Initial telemetry: connection resets down ~60%, tail latency improved. Still seeing intermittent failures from a handful of prefixes.

oncall-nyc: shifting 45% of non-critical traffic off az7 now; traffic smooths. Note: warmup for az6 backends ok.

customer-success: received two SE escalations asking for ETA and affected customer list. I shared current impacted ASNs and the status page link.

platform-sre: monitoring for 20 minutes before full rollback of routing. If stable, we'll keep MSS clamp as safety for 24 hours while neteng traces the upstream provider path.

neteng: next steps: open ticket with cloud provider peering team for upstream router MTU misconfiguration (likely jumbo-negotiation mismatch). Requesting traceroute and MTU probing from their edge to our LB. Also we should add PMTUD diagnostic probes to our synthetic checks.

oncall-eu: handing over to daytime oncall for monitoring and customer follow-ups. Summary for handoff emailed to #oncall-handoff: "INC-1768501123: IPv6 PMTUD blackhole in az7; MSS clamp + traffic shift mitigated majority of errors; provider ticket open; support updating customers; postmortem owner: @neteng."

neteng: I can own postmortem. Will collect PCAPs, route configs, and provider responses. Proposing RCA: upstream MTU mismatch + lack of ICMPv6 forwarding for PMTUD.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1768501123 status changed to MONITORING. :white_check_mark:

oncall-eu: thanks team. If anything regresses, re-pager.

support-ops: will follow up with impacted customers tomorrow with more detail and mitigation steps.

customer-success: noted. passing to account teams now.
